SUBJECT:  Public Works Week & Logo Resolutions

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Adopting a Resolution declaring the week of May 21 through 27, 2023 as Public
  Works Week in Monterey Park;
  2. Adopting a Resolution adopting a Public Works logo to be used by the Public
  Works Department for official purposes; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The City is celebrating the week of May 21-27, 2023, as Public Works Week in Monterey
Park. This week marks the 63rd annual National Public Works Week sponsored by the
American Public Works Association, which recognizes Public Works professionals. The
2023 National Public Works Week theme is “Connecting the World through Public Works”,
highlighting the way public works professionals connect us physically, through
infrastructure, and inspirationally, through service to their communities, whether as first
responders, or daily workers carrying out their duties with pride.

BACKGROUND:
The City of Monterey Park recognizes and celebrates the hard work, commitment and
contribution Public Works professionals provide to the community of Monterey Park. This
year, the City is hosting a Public Works Open House on Thursday, May 25, 2023 from
11:00 am to 1:30 pm at the City Yard located on 751 South Alhambra Avenue. The
"Connecting to the World through Public Works" theme focuses on how Public works
connectors help keep communities, like Monterey Park, strong by providing an
infrastructure of services in transportation, water, wastewater, and stormwater treatment,
public buildings and spaces, parks and grounds, emergency management and first
response, solid waste, and right-of-way management. Public works is the thread that
connects us all, with dedicated team members that strive to improve the quality of life for
the Monterey Park residents they serve, leading to healthier, happier communities.

In recognizing the Public Works department as an integral unit within the City’s
organization, it is recommend that an official Public Works logo be adopted to be used for
department promotional purposes. The proposed Public Works logo has been utilized for

SUBJECT:  Tree Memorial Program Recommendation for Fred Sornoso

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Authorizing the City Manager to take actions needed to honor
  former Mayor pro tem Fred Sornoso with a memorial tree; and
  2. Taking such additional, related action that may be desirable.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
At the April 29th City Council meeting, the City Council nominated former Mayor pro
tem Fred Sornoso for the Tree Memorial Recognition Program for his dedication and
service to the community. Tree Memorial honorees are nominated based on the
criteria established in Resolution Nos. 10485 and 11484 (Attachment 1).

If approved by City Council, Mr. Fred Sornoso will be honored with a Tree Memorial for
his service and positive impact on the Monterey Park community.

BACKGROUND:
Mr. Fred Sornoso was a Monterey Park resident for many years and contributed
countless hours of dedicated service to the community. Fred was known for his fierce
devotion to helping others and looking out for his Monterey Park neighbors. He
promoted community collaboration and fostered friendship and goodwill. Fred was also
known for his kindness and great sense of humor. The support of his neighbors was
made apparent when Fred was elected to represent District 3 on the Monterey Park City
Council. Mr. Sornoso was sworn into office as a Monterey Park City Councilmember on
April 1, 2020. Resolution No. 2022-R26 (Attachment 2) is attached as a reference of
Fred’s outstanding public service to the Monterey Park community.

During this time on City Council, Fred showcased his love for baseball and the Los
Angeles Dodgers by spearheading the annual MPK Night at Dodger Stadium. Fred also
helped to establish the annual Jr. MLB Homerun Derby and numerous
Community Clean up events. Due to his health, Mr. Sornoso relinquished his seat
as Mayor pro tem, on April 14, 2022, the 2022 season home opener at Dodger
Stadium.

Fred Sornoso was born on August 15, 1955, and passed away on July 8, 2022.

  regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regulations §§15000,

  collectively referred to as “CEQA Regulations.”

13.12.020. Definitions.

  Unless the contrary is stated or clearly appears from the context, the
  following definitions will govern the construction of the words and phrases
  used in this chapter:

  A.  “Administrator” means the public works director, or designee.

  B.  “Encroachment” means any construction work performed within public

  construction work performed within a public right-of-way or public service

  A.  Permit Required. Unless otherwise provided by applicable law, it is

13.12.040. Planting Vegetation.

CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
This Ordinance was reviewed pursuant to CEQA. Adopting this Ordinance is exempt from
further environmental review because it establishes rules and procedures for operation
of existing facilities; minor temporary use of land; minor alterations in land use; new
construction of small structures; and minor structures accessory to existing commercial
facilities. The Ordinance, therefore, is categorically exempt from further environmental
review under CEQA Guidelines §§ 15301; 15303, 15304(e); 15305; and 15311. Further,
adopting the ordinance is exempt from environmental review pursuant to CEQA
Guidelines § 15061(b)(3) because the ordinance is for general policies and procedure-
making. It can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the Ordinance may
have a significant effect on the environment. Individual projects utilizing these regulations
will each be separately subject to an environmental assessment. Finally, this Ordinance
is exempt from further environmental review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines § 15269(a)
because the protection of public and private property is necessary to maintain service
essential to the public, health and welfare.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
MPMC Chapter 13.12 regulates encroachments and construction within all public right of
ways within the City. The regulations under this chapter were first implemented in the
1980s and are stale in comparison to industry standards. The proposed ordinance
updates regulations for excavations and encroachments on, over, and under public rights-
of-ways and public service easements.

BACKGROUND:
Government Code Section 38775 permits the City to regulate and prohibit encroachments
into and obstructions on public property. An encroachment includes, without limitation,
the following:
   Any construction work performed within public rights-of-ways or public service
  easements;
   Any work other than construction work performed within a public right-of-way or
  public service easement that obstructs, or interferes with the use of, the public
  right-of-way or public service easement; and
   Any structure or object that is placed or installed within a public right-of-way or
  within a public service easement in a manner that obstructs or otherwise interferes
  with the use of the public right-of-way or public service easement.

The proposed ordinance repeals and replaces current provisions and procedures under
MPMC Chapter 13.12 and provides new permit requirements, including, exceptions to
permits, procedures for permit application process, permit insurance requirements,
guidelines for excavation in recently resurfaced public streets, requirements for traffic
control plans and procedures for administrative review of permit decisions. The Ordinance
also includes an encroachment permit application form and general conditions of approval
applicable to all encroachments in the City.

RECOMMENDATION:

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The California Energy Commission’s CalAPP Grant Program, funded by $20 million from
the California Budget Act of 2021 authorized by Senate Bill 129, is intended to help cities
and counties establish an online, automated solar permitting system. The City qualifies
for a $60,000 grant to reimburse the City for staff or consultant time associated with
implementing the solar permitting software, among others. Expediting solar permits will
help the City comply with the Solar Access Act and will advance the City’s Going Green
efforts towards promoting sustainability within the City.

The application deadline was May 1, 2023 and funds are awarded on a first-come, first-
served basis. Staff submitted our CalAPP Program Grant application on April 19, 2023
to meet this deadline. This is a reimbursable grant that allows for reimbursements through
May 1, 2027.

lf adopted, the proposed resolution would retroactively authorize the City Manager, or
designee, to apply for the CalAPP Program Grant, to execute the grant agreement, and
to implement a budget amendment if the City is awarded funds.

BACKGROUND:
In July 2021, $20 million from the California Budget Act of 2021, which was authorized by
Senate Bill 129, was appropriated to the California Energy Commission to support a grant
program to help cities and counties implement an online, automated solar permitting
system.

  Page 322 of 412

In September 2022, the Solar Access Act was passed through Senate Bill 379, which
requires that cities and counties automate the permitting process for certain solar
installation projects by September 30, 2023 (for cities and counties with populations
greater than 50,000). This is intended to cut down the cost and wait times for obtaining
a solar permit from cities.

The U.S. Department of Energy developed a solar permitting software called SolarAPP+.
This software will integrate with cities existing permitting software, is aimed at
streamlining and automating applications, standardizes plans for most solar applications
and provides an inspection checklist to assist with inspections.

The California Energy Commission administers the CalAPP Program Grant which is
intended to assist local governments recover the cost of establishing an automated,
online solar permitting system, including SolarAPP+ or a similar software. This grant can
be used to reimburse staff or consultant time associated with implementing the solar
permitting software, among others.

The maximum grant amount that a city can apply for is based on the latest estimated
population available from the California Department of Finance (DOF). According to
DOF’s estimates, the City’s population is 60,207 as of January 1, 2022. Cities with
populations between 50,000 to 99,999 qualify for grant funding up to $60,000 on a first-
come, first-served basis. The deadline to apply was May 1, 2023. Staff submitted our
CalAPP Program Grant application to implement the SolarApp+ software on April 19,
2023 to meet this deadline. The City received an email on April 20, 2023 indicating that
staff reviewed our application and is recommending approval by the Energy Commission.

FISCAL IMPACT:
The City may be granted up to $60,000 from the California Energy Commission to
establish an online, automated solar permitting system. If grant funds are received, the
attached resolution would allow the Finance Department to appropriate these funds.

  BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Monterey Park as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A. May is Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) Heritage Month.

  B. May 18, 2023 would have been Vincent Chin’s 68th birthday. Vincent Chin was

  short when two men brutally attacked him. His murder fueled a national Asian
  American activist movement that continues to this day.

  C. There has been a rise in bullying, discrimination, and hate crimes against the
  Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) community since the start of the
  COVID-19 pandemic.

  D. Every day, kids of all ages suffer from being bullied in schools and online across
  the United States.

  E. In the AAPI community, this problem is often compounded by cultural, religious,
  and linguistic barriers that can keep youth from seeking and receiving help. And
  certain AAPI groups – including South Asian, Muslim, Sikh, Micronesian,
  LGBTQ+, immigrant, and limited English proficient youth – are more likely to
  be the targets of bullying.

Bullying and Hate.

dedicated to fighting bullying for Asian American and Pacific Islander youth) in sharing
one vision - a world where all youth, including AAPI youth, have the opportunity to grow
up feeling proud and supported in the development of their identities and sharing of their
stories. The City of Monterey Park is committed to this important issue and encourages
the public to foster dialogue, share resources, and learn more about what they can do to
end bullying.

  The City’s auditor, CliftonLarsonAllen LLP (CLA), an independent auditor and one

  statements for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2022. The audited financial
  statements are incorporated into an ACFR.

  unmodified (“clean”) opinion on the City’s financial statements. An unmodified
  opinion indicates that the financial data of the City is fairly presented in accordance
  with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (or
  “GAAP”) and the standards applicable to the financial audits contained in
  Government Audit Standards, issued by the Comptroller General of the United
  States. These standards require that the auditors plan and perform the audit to
  obtain reasonable assurance as to whether the financial statements are free of
  material misstatement and accurately reflects the City’s financial position.
  Additionally, the auditors’ report does not indicate any negative findings, internal
  control deficiencies or instances of noncompliance with applicable laws and
  regulations.

3-D.  LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT

  A Land Acknowledgment is a statement that recognizes and respects Indigenous
  Peoples as traditional stewards of lands, expresses gratitude and appreciation to
  those groups, and honors the Indigenous people who have lived and worked on
  the land for centuries. Land Acknowledgments are a common practice in both
  Australia and Canada and are increasingly being adopted by city, county, and state
  governments in the United States.

  Staff met with representatives from the Gabrieleño/Tongva San Gabriel Band of
  Mission Indians to learn more about their recommendations for Land
  Acknowledgment language and practices. Based on our discussions, staff
  proposes the following Land Acknowledgment statement which has been reviewed
  and approved by the Gabrieleño/Tongva San Gabriel Band of Mission Indians:

  We would like to acknowledge that the land we inhabit today was once known
  as Tovangaar, the home of the Gabrieleño-Tongva people. We show our
  respect to the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, as well as all Indigenous people,
  past, present, and future, and honor their labor as original caretakers of this
  land. We commit to uplifting the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, invite you to
  acknowledge the history, and join us in caring for this land.

  Public Speakers:

  -  Mona Morales Recalde, member of the San Gabriel Band of Mission Indians,
  partnered with the City to draft a Land Acknowledgement statement. She stated
  that this statement acknowledges that the ancestral land in which the City is on
  is Gabrieleño/Tongva land. She requested the City Council’s consideration in
  adopting the Land Acknowledgement.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved and adopted a Land Acknowledgement
  statement as amended to add the Land Acknowledgement language to all public
  meeting agendas and for it to be read at city events.

3-E.  NATIONAL CORRECTIONAL OFFICERS WEEK RESOLUTION

  The Monterey Park Police Department is celebrating the week of May 7-13, 2023,
  as National Correctional Officers Week. In 1984, President Ronald Regan
  announced the first week in May as National Correctional Officers Week, and it
  has been celebrated annually ever since. It honors the thousands of men and
  women responsible for managing those brought into custody by law enforcement
  and awaiting trial. These individuals face difficult and often dangerous work
  environments and play a vital role in the criminal justice system. We are enlisting
  your support in the form of a resolution to honor these men and women in our area
  for their work every day to protect the residents of Monterey Park.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R30 declaring the
  week of May 7-13, 2023 to be National Correctional Officers Week in the City of
  Monterey Park, on Consent Calendar.

3-F.  NATIONAL POLICE WEEK RESOLUTION

  The Monterey Park Police Department is celebrating the week of May 15-21, 2023,
  as National Police Week. In 1962, President John F. Kennedy proclaimed May 15th
  as National Peace Officers Memorial Day and the calendar week in which May 15th
  falls, as National Police Week. National Police Week pays special recognition to
  those law enforcement officers who have lost their lives in the line of duty for the
  safety and protection of others and is a collaborative effort of many organizations
  dedicated to honoring America’s law enforcement community. We are enlisting
  your support in the form of a resolution to honor these men and women in our area
  for the work that they do every day to protect the residents of Monterey Park.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R31 declaring the
  week of May 15-21, 2023 to be National Police Week in the City of Monterey Park.

  ITS ENTIRETY TO REGULATE ENCROACHMENTS WITHIN THE PUBLIC
  RIGHT-OF-WAY

  MPMC Chapter 13.12 regulates encroachments and construction within all public
  right of ways within the City. The regulations under this chapter were first
  implemented in the 1980s and are stale in comparison to industry standards. The
  proposed ordinance updates regulations for excavations and encroachments on,
  over, and under public rights-of-ways and public service easements.

  The Ordinance was introduced and received first reading at the April 19, 2023 City
  Council meeting. The original staff report (from April 19, 2023) is attached to the

3-J.  CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION CALIFORNIA AUTOMATED PERMIT
  PROCESSING (CALAPP) PROGRAM GRANT

  The California Energy Commission’s CalAPP Grant Program, funded by $20
  million from the California Budget Act of 2021 authorized by Senate Bill 129, is
  intended to help cities and counties establish an online, automated solar permitting
  system. The City qualifies for a $60,000 grant to reimburse the City for staff or
  consultant time associated with implementing the solar permitting software, among
  others. Expediting solar permits will help the City comply with the Solar Access Act
  and will advance the City’s Going Green efforts towards promoting sustainability
  within the City.

  The application deadline was May 1, 2023 and funds are awarded on a first-come,
  first-served basis. Staff submitted our CalAPP Program Grant application on April
  19, 2023 to meet this deadline. This is a reimbursable grant that allows for
  reimbursements through May 1, 2027.

  If adopted, the proposed resolution would retroactively authorize the City Manager,
  or designee, to apply for the CalAPP Program Grant, to execute the grant
  agreement, and to implement a budget amendment if the City is awarded funds.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R34 retroactively
  authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to apply for, receive, and appropriate
  grant funds for the California Energy Commission’s California Automated Permit
  Processing (CalAPP) Program Grant, on Consent Calendar.
